planning_notes: Preserve the authoritative wiring: heater D10, fan D5, buzzer D6, DHT11 D7, TM1637 CLK D4 and DIO D3, LED D13, and button D2. No additional remapping is required.
Implement heater hysteresis in SysML: turn on below 37 Celsius, turn off above 38 Celsius, and retain the previous command within the band. The setpoint is 37.5 Celsius.
Implement ventilation for 10 seconds every 300 seconds, with the fan also running above 38 Celsius. Assume the first scheduled ventilation starts 300 seconds after initialization.

Use actual elapsed time for ventilation and the continuous 60000 ms out-of-band persistence timer. Returning to the inclusive 37–38 Celsius band resets the timer. Threshold comparisons, alarm transitions, and timing remain model logic.

Use the legal default DHT11 sampling interval, shared by temperature and validity and no shorter than 2000 ms. Invalid acquisitions retain the previous temperature but must not be treated as fresh valid measurements.

Startup assumptions: heater, fan, alarm, and LED are off; current-temperature display mode is selected, and the display remains blank until a valid measurement is available. Setup must not wait for the first DHT acquisition.
Assume each debounced press toggles between current temperature and setpoint. Round the selected value to the nearest whole Celsius in SysML; reflect accepted button events within 250 ms.
The LED function and audible alarm frequency are unspecified. Assume the LED follows the persistent alarm and the buzzer sounds continuously at 1000 Hz while that alarm is active.
Assume the exact fixed serial line is emitted once on each transition into the persistent alarm state, at 9600 baud. No serial receiver or additional numeric reporting is required.
Relay and fan electrical polarity are unspecified, so use catalog defaults. Button wiring follows the authorized INPUT_PULLUP-to-GND default, with no second inversion of its normalized pressed value.

Invalid-sensor safety behavior remains a model-policy question: resolve heater handling, persistence-timer handling, and alarm clearing during invalid acquisitions explicitly rather than making decisions from retained measurements.

The contract binds DHT11 temperature/validity to D7, heater to D10, fan to D5, buzzer to D6, TM1637 to CLK D4/DIO D3, LED to D13, and button to D2. The explicit DIO remapping resolves the original collision. D13 is active HIGH and initially OFF; D2 uses INPUT_PULLUP with LOW normalized to pressed, which the model consumes without reinversion. Timer state starts at zero. Heating uses strict below-37 and above-38 comparisons and retains its command within the inclusive band. Ventilation uses actual elapsed milliseconds for 10000-ms windows every 300000 ms, initially waiting one period; valid overtemperature also commands the fan. Consecutive valid out-of-band observations accumulate elapsed time to 60000 ms; valid in-band readings reset persistence and clear the alarm. Alarm activation selects the tone and LED and produces a one-step gate for the registered exact serial message at 9600 baud. Rising button edges toggle mode, including a first sampled press, without repeated toggles while held. Display selection rounds current temperature or the 37.5 Celsius setpoint to whole Celsius. Model updates precede output evaluation; 10-ms button, controller, and output periods introduce no modeled violation of the 250-ms command/display bounds. requirement_checks.requirement_quote: 构建一个智能孵化箱控制系统，使用 DHT11（D7）、加热器继电器 D10、风扇 D5、蜂鸣器 D6、TM1637（CLK=D4，DIO=D3）、LED D13 和按钮 D2。
requirement_checks.reason: All SOURCE-1 clauses were reviewed, including the resolved configuration and operational acceptance profile. The contract binds DHT11 temperature/validity to D7, heater to D10, fan to D5, buzzer to D6, TM1637 to CLK D4/DIO D3, LED to D13, and button to D2. The explicit DIO remapping resolves the original collision. D13 is active HIGH and initially OFF; D2 uses INPUT_PULLUP with LOW normalized to pressed, which the model consumes without reinversion. Timer state starts at zero. Heating uses strict below-37 and above-38 comparisons and retains its command within the inclusive band. Ventilation uses actual elapsed milliseconds for 10000-ms windows every 300000 ms, initially waiting one period; valid overtemperature also commands the fan. Consecutive valid out-of-band observations accumulate elapsed time to 60000 ms; valid in-band readings reset persistence and clear the alarm. Alarm activation selects the tone and LED and produces a one-step gate for the registered exact serial message at 9600 baud. Rising button edges toggle mode, including a first sampled press, without repeated toggles while held. Display selection rounds current temperature or the 37.5 Celsius setpoint to whole Celsius. Model updates precede output evaluation; 10-ms button, controller, and output periods introduce no modeled violation of the 250-ms command/display bounds. The 2000-ms DHT sampling period does not introduce an additional delay after a reading becomes available. No continuous Boolean Serial stream or numeric DHT Serial stream is requested, so the conditional continuous-stream defaults do not require additional reports. Neither model nor contract requires setup to wait for a reading or timer; the 500-ms setup requirement is consistent at this boundary, with execution verification deferred.

requirement_checks.requirement_quote: Temperature outside either bound continuously for 60 seconds raises the alarm; returning inside the band resets that persistence timer.
requirement_checks.reason: All R1 clauses were reviewed. The registered interfaces preserve the requested devices and authoritative DIO D3 resolution explicitly authorized alongside the original D5 wiring. Valid temperatures below 37 Celsius enable heating, temperatures above 38 disable it, and values from 37 through 38 retain the previous heater command. The fan combines overtemperature cooling with elapsed-time-driven ventilation. Its phase wraps at 300000 ms, and phase values below 10000 enable ventilation after the initial full-period wait; the contract's first elapsed delta is zero, so initial enable sequencing discards no elapsed time. The first out-of-band observation establishes onset without charging the preceding interval. Subsequent consecutive out-of-band steps accumulate actual elapsed time, saturating at 60000 ms. Ordered updates allow alarm activation on the threshold-reaching step. Returning to either inclusive boundary or the interior resets the timer and clears the alarm. reportRaised is cleared each step and asserted only upon alarm entry, yielding one exact 'incubation abnormal' line per episode under the registered level-sensitive serial semantics, at 9600 baud. The alarm drives a 1000-Hz tone and LED. Rising normalized D2 presses toggle display mode once per press; held input retains mode. Current readings use floor(temperature + 0.5), and setpoint mode selects 38, consistently representing 37.5 as whole Celsius. Current mode initially precedes any press, and the display remains blank until a valid reading. Invalid readings turn heating off, prevent cooling from retained data, reset incomplete persistence, retain the last valid displayed temperature, and leave an existing alarm latched until a valid in-band reading; R1 specifies no conflicting invalid-data policy. Ventilation and button processing remain independent of sensor validity. These conclusions derive from model logic and contract bindings, not from the supplied test descriptions.

limitations: Satisfied checks establish model-boundary consistency, not runtime success. The supplied test descriptions are not executed evidence.
